details: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed to secure the necessary 60 votes to proceed in the U.S. Senate on September 15, 2026. This legislative setback prolongs regulatory uncertainty for the U.S. crypto industry, contributing to a cautious market reaction. Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced declines following the vote.
title: US Senate Crypto Clarity Act Fails to Advance

details: Market-implied odds for a 25 basis point Federal Reserve interest rate hike on September 16, 2026, surged to over 85%. This increase in hawkish sentiment is partly attributed to attacks on Saudi pipeline infrastructure, which pushed crude oil prices significantly higher and amplified inflation concerns in the U.S. Higher interest rates typically reduce the attractiveness of non-yielding assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Fed Rate Hike Odds Jump Amid Oil Spike and Inflation Concerns

details: On September 14, 2026, the U.S. Treasury, under "Operation Economic Outcast," sanctioned a major bank for facilitating Iran's evasion of sanctions. The Treasury warned that any entity involved in money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system, indicating an accelerated pace of enforcement.
title: US Sanctions Major Bank for Iran Sanctions Evasion

details: The U.S. is pursuing a civil forfeiture claim for $61 million in cryptocurrency allegedly linked to Iran's black-market oil sales. In response, crypto exchange Binance stated its strict prohibition of transactions with sanctioned entities and confirmed cooperation with law enforcement by freezing suspicious accounts. This action highlights ongoing efforts to combat illicit financial activities involving digital assets.
title: US Seeks Forfeiture of $61M Crypto Tied to Iran Oil Sales
